ai-at-work.title: What ClickUp’s mass layoff tells us about the future of work
ai-at-work.excerpt: The nine-year-old startup is replacing hundreds of employees with thousands of AI agents.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: ClickUp laid off hundreds of workers and replaced them with AI agents to handle routine tasks across their platform. This matters because it's a real-world test case of what AI automation actually looks like at scale, not the theoretical stuff we read about in vendor whitepapers. Here's the thing though: if ClickUp can't figure out how to keep humans in the loop while automating grunt work, they're probably building something nobody actually wants to use, because work still requires judgment calls that AI currently botches.

ai-at-work.title: The pope’s AI encyclical isn’t really about AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical uses AI as a lens to diagnose older problems: concentrated power, eroding democracy, and a tech elite that shapes the world to its own advantage.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The Pope's latest encyclical uses artificial intelligence as a vehicle to address deeper structural problems like power concentration, democratic erosion, and tech oligarchy rather than focusing narrowly on AI itself. This matters to digital workplace leaders because it's a reminder that the tools we implement don't exist in a vacuum, and blindly adopting the latest technology without examining who benefits and who loses is exactly how we end up with workplace systems that entrench inequality. Turns out even the Vatican knows that "it's not actually about the technology" is the most important lesson in digital transformation, which is either comforting or deeply depressing depending on how many failed AI pilots you've already watched.

ai-at-work.title: Ferrari is using IBM’s AI to create F1 superfans
ai-at-work.excerpt: IBM and Scuderia Ferrari HP take TechCrunch inside how they are redefining the fan experience.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Ferrari partnered with IBM to deploy AI tools that personalize fan experiences and engagement around Formula 1 racing. This matters because it shows how major organizations are moving beyond internal productivity AI and actually using it to create differentiated customer experiences that drive real business value. The funny part is that Ferrari needed IBM's help to figure out how to talk to fans, which suggests even legendary brands recognize that throwing technology at engagement problems without proper strategy is just expensive window dressing.

ai-at-work.title: Railway secures $100 million to challenge AWS with AI-native cloud infrastructure
ai-at-work.excerpt: Railway, a San Francisco-based cloud platform that has quietly amassed two million developers without spending a dollar on marketing, announced Thursday that it raised $100 million in a Series B fundi
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Railway just raised $100 million to build AI-focused cloud infrastructure that challenges AWS's dominance. This matters because your current cloud setup might not handle AI workloads efficiently, and having real alternatives to AWS forces the big players to actually compete instead of just raising prices every quarter. Honestly, it's refreshing to see someone building for what companies actually need now instead of what worked in 2015.

tools-tech.title: Google adds open source Agent Executor to support AI agents in production
tools-tech.excerpt: Google has introduced Agent Executor, an open source runtime aimed at helping enterprises run AI agents more reliably at scale, as attention shifts from building agent prototypes to managing the opera
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google released Agent Executor, an open source tool designed to help companies actually run AI agents in production instead of just building proof-of-concepts that sit in a lab somewhere. This matters because if you're betting on AI agents to handle real work in your organization, you need infrastructure that doesn't fall apart when things get messy at scale. Honestly, it's refreshing to see Google acknowledge that the hard part isn't the AI itself, it's keeping the lights on when your agent decides to go rogue at 2 a.m.

tools-tech.title: Q&A: How video helps build robot brains for physical AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Robots could well be the next trillion-dollar tech opportunity, in no small part thanks to AI. Not surprisingly, that’s led to race by a variety of robotics companies to build industrial and humanoid
tools-tech.dwp_take: Robotics companies are training AI models by feeding them millions of YouTube videos so robots can understand physical spaces and perform tasks in the real world. This matters to digital workplace professionals because we're about to manage workplaces where robots are actual colleagues, which means rethinking everything from network infrastructure to physical space design. Honestly, we spent years optimizing offices for Zoom calls only to discover the real threat was always the machines learning to navigate them better than we do.

tools-tech.title: FBI warns of Kali Oauth stealers
tools-tech.excerpt: The FBI has warned of the danger from a new wave of phishing attacks generated by a tool called Kali365. It enables cyber criminals to obtain Microsoft 365 access tokens and bypass multi-factor authen
tools-tech.dwp_take: The FBI is warning about Kali365, a tool that lets attackers steal Microsoft 365 OAuth tokens through phishing, effectively bypassing MFA without needing actual passwords. This matters because your users are your weakest link, and even solid MFA doesn't protect against token theft if someone clicks a malicious link. The real takeaway here is that MFA alone won't save you, so you need proper email filtering, user training that actually sticks, and monitoring for suspicious token activity.

tools-tech.title: Meta says goodbye to those who won’t use AI
tools-tech.excerpt: Meta is the latest company to trim its workforce as a result of the growing use of AI within the industry. The company laid off 8,000 employees earlier this week, while also moving 7,000 more to AI-fo
tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta just fired 8,000 people and shuffled 7,000 others into AI roles, basically saying "learn to work with AI or find the door." This matters because it's a real signal that enterprise software and workplace tools are about to change fast, and your training budget better account for people who need to actually understand these systems rather than just fear them. Here's the thing though: moving people to "AI-focused roles" doesn't magically make them useful if you haven't thought through what those roles actually do.

digital-culture.title: How AI keeps both job seekers and employers from filling roles
digital-culture.excerpt: Jobseekers and recruiters are at a technological standoff. Candidates upload (and retype) their resumes into an applicant tracking system (ATS) with no sense of whether or not their applications are g
digital-culture.dwp_take: AI-powered applicant tracking systems are screening out qualified candidates at scale while job seekers game the system with keyword stuffing and resume tricks, creating a mutual frustration loop. This matters because your talent pipeline is only as good as the tools filtering it, and right now those tools are broken in ways that hurt both sides. The irony is that companies spent millions on automation to solve hiring problems and somehow made them worse, which tells you everything you need to know about implementing technology without understanding the actual human workflow first.

digital-culture.title: Bosses take remote less work seriously when it’s geared toward parents, study shows
digital-culture.excerpt: Being penalized for using flexible working policies—remote work, hybrid work, parental leave, and more—can be subtle, or screamingly obvious. Nicole Yelland, a communications strategist from Detroit,
digital-culture.dwp_take: A new study confirms what most of us already know: managers take remote work less seriously when employees cite parenting responsibilities, essentially punishing people for being honest about why they need flexibility. This matters because it exposes the gap between stated DEI commitments and actual behavior, and it means your organization is probably losing talented people to competitors who don't penalize honesty. Here's the real kicker: managers who treat parental flexibility as less legitimate than "I just want to work from home" are basically admitting they've got no actual trust framework for remote work, which is a management problem dressed up as a flexibility problem.

digital-culture.title: AI is already killing the executive assistant job
digital-culture.excerpt: There is a growing body of evidence that AI is redefining white-collar work. It’s not just the endless rounds of layoffs at tech companies that herald this transformation. Entry-level jobs are disappe
digital-culture.dwp_take: AI automation is eliminating executive assistant roles faster than anyone predicted, with entry-level positions across white-collar sectors disappearing alongside them. This matters because your workplace is about to lose institutional knowledge sitting in those assistant roles, and you'll discover too late that nobody documented where anything actually lives. The irony is that most executives will spend the next two years looking for their own passwords while wondering why their calendar is a disaster.

digital-culture.title: AI may be eating jobs, but it poses an even bigger threat
digital-culture.excerpt: The AI conversation today focuses on systems. Which jobs will survive? How does education need to adapt? What happens to the economy when machines produce what humans used to? Governments are commissi
digital-culture.dwp_take: Researchers are warning that while job displacement from AI gets all the attention, the real threat is something we can actually control: how we prepare people and systems to work alongside these tools right now. For digital workplace leaders, this means stopping the endless "AI will destroy work" handwringing and starting concrete work on skills training, process redesign, and cultural readiness in your organization today. The irony is that most companies will get blindsided not by AI itself, but by their own paralysis while waiting for the perfect strategy to emerge.

industry-news.excerpt: Southwest banned human-like and animal-like robots from cabins and checked baggage after viral flights raised concerns about lithium-ion battery safety. The post Southwest Bans Humanoid Robots After V
industry-news.dwp_take: Southwest Airlines decided to ban humanoid and animal-like robots from passenger cabins and checked baggage due to safety concerns around lithium-ion batteries after some viral moments got people's attention.
